content:
The Observatory forecasts that today's maximum outdoor temperature will reach 34 degrees Celsius, approaching the 34.9 degrees recorded on the 'Major Heat' day in 2022, about 4 degrees higher than last year's 'Major Heat'.

The Observatory continues to issue the Very Hot Weather Warning, forecasting that today will be mainly sunny, but with showers in some areas from morning to noon, and extremely high temperatures during the day. In addition, affected by the subtropical ridge, Hong Kong will be generally sunny, but coastal areas will also be affected by showers.

The heat wave triggered by 'Major Heat' made the streets of Hong Kong stuffy like an oven, with a thermometer at Mong Kok MacPherson Playground recording a high of 40.8 degrees.

In the past, on 'Major Heat' days, the highest temperature was 34.9 degrees in 2022, and the lowest was 22.2 degrees in 1965.

In addition, the highest average relative humidity and highest total rainfall recorded on 'Major Heat' days over the years were 96% in 1994 and 195.1 millimetres respectively; while the lowest average relative humidity was 70% in 1968.
